message.content:
My Dearest Family,

I am writing this by the flickering light of a single oil lamp, my hands still trembling slightly from the cold and the sheer force of what we have endured. The ship is finally quiet, save for the gentle creaking of the wood as it settles into the calm waters of the morning. I know you must be worried, perhaps even terrified, hearing the news of the storm that swept through our sector last night. I need you to know, with every fiber of my being, that I am safe. We are all safe.

It began with a strange, heavy silence in the air, a pressure that made my ears pop and my skin prickle. The sky turned a bruised purple, and the wind began to howl with a voice I have never heard before. It was not just a gale; it was a fury. The waves rose like mountains, towering above our masts, crashing down with a violence that shook the very bones of the ship. For hours, it felt as though the ocean itself was trying to swallow us whole. The rain lashed against the deck like gravel, and the lightning split the sky so brightly that I could see the white foam of the waves in the dark.
